- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >2.5x recent mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or 2.5x prior 7-day average.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 5–15% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 30-day forecast by averaging with 18-day history if sentiment volatility > 0.4.
- For horizon > 14 days, model tends to underestimate; apply 10–15% upward bias if sentiment remains neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model exhibits oscillation bias; dampen forecast by 5–10% for next 7 days.
